nodes.title: Windows MSIX/AppX: Chromium GPU process can be killed when Code Integrity rejects vk_swiftshader.dll
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

An Electron/Chromium application packaged as MSIX/AppX should be able to initialize its GPU process without Windows terminating the process because a bundled Chromium runtime DLL does not satisfy the effective binary-signature policy.

If SwiftShader cannot be loaded under the GPU process's Code Integrity policy, Chromium should fall back gracefully rather than causing the GPU process — and potentially the entire packaged application — to terminate.

### Actual Behavior

There are now independent reports from multiple packaged Chromium/Electron desktop applications where the Chromium GPU process attempts to load:

```text
vk_swiftshader.dll
```

and Windows records Code Integrity Event ID 3033:

```text
Code Integrity determined that a process (...) attempted to load
...\vk_swiftshader.dll
that did not meet the Microsoft signing level requirements.
```

This is followed by the GPU process terminating and, in several reproductions, failing to relaunch.

Typical Chromium logs include:

```text
GPU process exited unexpectedly
GPU process launch failed
GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.
```

On affected MSIX installations, the package can additionally transition to:

```text
Modified, NeedsRemediation
```

after which the application may no longer launch until repaired/reinstalled.

### Evidence that MSIX/AppX execution is relevant

One OpenAI Codex reproduction copied the exact same application payload out of:

```text
C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\...
```

and executed it from an ordinary directory.

Results:

```text
Packaged MSIX:
Code Integrity 3033 on vk_swiftshader.dll
application terminated

Same files executed unpackaged:
normal GPU path works
no Code Integrity block
application remains running
```

This suggests that the packaged execution environment / GPU child-process signing policy is material to the failure.

A separate Claude Desktop report reproduced the problem 15/15 times using the MSIX build while the same-version non-MSIX build worked.

WinDbg on the Claude GPU child showed:

```text
ntdll!LdrAppxHandleIntegrityFailure
```

with Code Integrity simultaneously rejecting `vk_swiftshader.dll`.

### Code Integrity details

Another independent Codex reproduction recorded:

```text
Event ID: 3033
DLL: vk_swiftshader.dll
Status: 0xC0000428
RequestedPolicy: 8
ValidatedPolicy: 1
```

and observed the GPU child with:

```text
MicrosoftSignedOnly = ON
AllowStoreSignedBinaries = OFF
```

The Code Integrity event was immediately followed by the Chromium GPU process crashing and its relaunch failing.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

### Existing reports

OpenAI Codex:

https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/35505

https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/34133

https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/35352

https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/35681

https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/35635

Anthropic Claude Desktop:

https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/80999

https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/81341

There is an existing Electron GPU-sandbox issue:

https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/51761

but that issue appears to involve a different trigger: directory DACLs containing orphaned/zombie SIDs. I am including it only because the failure also occurs during Chromium GPU sandbox initialization; I do not believe it describes the same MSIX/Code Integrity failure.

### Chromium-related finding

One of the Codex reports points to Chromium change:

https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/963206a961a7992b048d07f756f87f11fa2e5420

concerning SwiftShader initialization/preloading around GPU sandbox startup.

I have not established whether this change completely resolves the MSIX/AppX case, but it may be relevant to determining whether the appropriate fix belongs in Electron, Chromium, ANGLE/SwiftShader, or application packaging.

### Minimal reproduction

I do not currently have a standalone Electron testcase.

A useful minimal reproduction would likely be:

1. Create a minimal Electron application with a `BrowserWindow`.
2. Package it as MSIX/AppX.
3. Launch it normally.
4. Trigger Chromium GPU initialization and a path that probes/falls back to SwiftShader.
5. Inspect:

```text
Applications and Services Logs
  Microsoft
    Windows
      CodeIntegrity
        Operational
```

6. Check for Event ID `3033` involving:

```text
vk_swiftshader.dll
```

7. Run the same Electron payload unpackaged as a control.

### Why I'm reporting this upstream

At this point I don't know whether the correct fix belongs in:

* Electron
* Chromium's GPU process / sandbox configuration
* ANGLE / SwiftShader
* MSIX/AppX binary signing/catalog handling
* application packaging configuration

However, the same failure mode is now independently documented in multiple Chromium/Electron packaged applications, with Code Integrity logs directly correlating `vk_swiftshader.dll` rejection with GPU-process termination.

I'm opening this primarily to determine whether Electron can reproduce this with a minimal packaged application and whether packaged Windows builds need different handling for Chromium's GPU-process binary-signature policy.

nodes.title: Electron Fuses for --no-stdio-init flag
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Electron fails to start when nul device are disabled on Windows. This issue has been reported in #44881 and fixed in #47870.

Current fix is ​​to start electron with the `--no-stdio-init` flag, but there is no way to always enable this flag. Because NodeJS has not been initialized, `app.relaunch` cannot work.

We could probably provide a fuse to always enable it. Otherwise, when the program is released and users experience program crashes, they will be helpless.

### Proposed Solution

Provide a fuse to always enable the `--no-stdio-init` flag

### Alternatives Considered

Use an external program to check if the NUL device is available and then start electron using the `--no-stdio-init` flag, but this requires introducing an additional build process.

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 43.3 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Other Linux ### Operating System Version CachyOS 7.1.6-1, GNOME 50.4 (Wayland) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version 43.2 ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior icon should appear on the top right through libappindicator when it is launched (and provides one) ### Actual Behavior three dots appear on the right side and the icon never loads ### Testcase Gist URL _No response_ ### Additional Information Upgrading from Electron 43.2.x to 43.3.0 causes AppIndicator/StatusNotifierItem tray icons to disappear on GNOME 50.4 (Wayland). This has been reproduced with at least Caprine and youtube-music-desktop-app by launching the app.asar with electron directly. Electron 43.2 works correctly for both applications when doing the same thing. The app registers a org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-* D-Bus name, but /StatusNotifierItem exports no interfaces: ```busctl --user introspect \ org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-XXXXX-1 \ /StatusNotifierItem NAME TYPE SIGNATURE RESULT/VALUE FLAGS ``` and running `gdbus introspect --session --dest org.freedesktop.StatusNotifierItem-XXXXX-1 --object-path /StatusNotifierItem ` returns the following: ``` node /StatusNotifierItem { }; ``` Downgrading to Electron 43.2 through electron43-bin in the AUR restores normal tray icon behavior.

nodes.title: BaseWindow.setBounds throws an exception if some of the properties of the `Rectangle` are missing
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.1.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

MacOS 27 (Golden Gate)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

unknown

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

[Documentation](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/base-window#winsetboundsbounds-animate) states that `BaseWindow::setBounds` accept `Partial<Rectangle>`.

This slightly modified example from docs should not throw any exceptions:

```ts
const { app, BaseWindow } = require('electron')

app.whenReady().then(() => {
  const win = new BaseWindow()

  // set all bounds properties
  win.setBounds({ x: 440, y: 225, width: 800, height: 600 })

  // set a single bounds property
  win.setBounds({ width: 100 })

  // { x: 440, y: 225, width: 100, height: 600 }
  console.log(win.getBounds())
})
```

### Actual Behavior

The provided example throws `UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning: TypeError: Error processing argument at index 0`.



### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Note, that it does not throw if I use `BrowserWindow` instead of `BaseWindow`.

nodes.title: Browser process aborts (NOTREACHED "Unsuitable process reused for site") when an MV3 extension service worker is re-woken via startWorkerForScope
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the Contributing Guidelines for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the Code of Conduct that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.0.0 (Chromium 150.0.7871.46)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.6 (25G72), arm64 (M3 Pro)

### What arch are you using?

arm64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown — first observed on 43.0.0. I have not bisected.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No. Chrome loads the same extension without incident. Note that Electron runs with
`--disable-features=SpareRendererForSitePerProcess`, which Chrome does not, and this
plausibly makes process reuse more aggressive here (see Additional Information).

### Expected Behavior

Waking a stopped MV3 extension background service worker — which
`session.serviceWorkers.startWorkerForScope()` does, and which
`electron-chrome-extensions` does on every `chrome.*` event delivery — should either
start the worker or fail gracefully.

### Actual Behavior

The **browser process** aborts with `EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)` on `CrBrowserMain`.
The whole app disappears; this is not a renderer crash and it is not catchable from
JavaScript.

The abort is a Chromium `NOTREACHED` in
`content/browser/renderer_host/render_process_host_impl.cc:5423`:

```cpp
if (render_process_host && !RenderProcessHostImpl::MayReuseAndIsSuitable(
                               render_process_host, site_instance)) {
  …
  NOTREACHED() << "Unsuitable process reused for site " << site_info;
}
```

Symbolicated stack (Breakpad symbols from the 43.0.0 release, framework UUID
`4C4C443A55553144A1ACB7F47BA94945`):

```
base::MessagePumpCFRunLoopBase::RunWorkSource
  mojo::internal::MultiplexRouter::Accept
    storage::mojom::ServiceWorkerStorageControl_FindRegistrationForScope_ForwardToCallback::Accept
      content::ServiceWorkerRegistry::DidFindRegistrationForScope
        content::ServiceWorkerContextWrapper::DidFindRegistrationForFindImpl
          content::(anonymous namespace)::FoundRegistrationForStartWorker
            content::ServiceWorkerVersion::StartWorker
              content::ServiceWorkerVersion::StartWorkerInternal
                content::EmbeddedWorkerInstance::Start                    (embedded_worker_instance.cc:289)
                  content::ServiceWorkerProcessManager::AllocateWorkerProcess (service_worker_process_manager.cc:145)
                    content::SiteInstanceImpl::GetOrCreateProcess            (site_instance_impl.cc:482)
                      content::RenderProcessHostImpl::GetProcessHostForSiteInstance
                        NOTREACHED()                                        (render_process_host_impl.cc:5423)
```

`FoundRegistrationForStartWorker` is referenced from exactly one function in
Chromium — `ServiceWorkerContextWrapper::StartWorkerForScope` — which is the backing
of `session.serviceWorkers.startWorkerForScope()`. So the crash is specific to that
API, not to service workers in general: a website's service worker starting through
navigation/fetch/push does not take this path.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

**Reproduction shape.** Load an MV3 extension with a background service worker into a
`persist:` session, then browse normally. The MV3 worker idles out after ~30s and is
re-woken on the next `chrome.*` event via `startWorkerForScope`. The crash happens on
one of those wakes. It is not deterministic per wake — many wakes succeed — but it
recurs reliably over a session. I have five crash reports with **byte-identical**
stacks (same image offsets in every frame), with uptimes from 2m22s to 2h14m.

I instrumented `session.serviceWorkers.on('running-status-changed')` to log the worker
lifecycle. The last events before one crash:

```
18:38:30.818Z stopping v0 chrome-extension://<id>/
18:38:30.820Z stopped  v0 chrome-extension://<id>/
   …crash 27 seconds later, mid-browsing, with no extension install/enable in between
```

No `starting` line is logged for the fatal wake, because the running-status observer
fires after process allocation — the abort happens first. A benign cycle earlier in
the same session shows `stopped` → `starting` 138 ms later, i.e. the same wake path
succeeding.

**Where I think it goes wrong.** `shell/browser/electron_browser_client.cc`
special-cases extensions in three process-model hooks:

- `ShouldUseProcessPerSite` returns true only for extensions, so the extension's
  service worker `SiteInstance` resolves through the process-per-site map.
- `DoesSiteRequireDedicatedProcess` returns true for extensions.
- `IsSuitableHost` compares a process "privilege" derived from
  `extensions::ProcessMap`.

My hypothesis is that after an MV3 worker stops, the process-per-site map still points
at the process that hosted the extension, while `extensions::ProcessMap` no longer
records that process as the extension's. The privilege comparison then fails,
`MayReuseAndIsSuitable` returns false, and the `NOTREACHED` fires. That would explain
the one distinguishing feature of this bug: it never fails on the worker's *first*
start, only on a later wake.

I have not verified that mechanism directly — the offending `site_info` is stored via
`SetCrashKeyString` and, in a release build, the streamed `NOTREACHED` message is
compiled out, so it does not reach stderr and macOS `.ips` files do not carry crash
keys. If a maintainer can point me at the right instrumentation I am happy to gather
more.

**Impact.** Any Electron app loading an MV3 extension is exposed, since
`electron-chrome-extensions` calls `startWorkerForScope` on every event delivery to a
stopped worker. The failure kills the browser process, so an app cannot defend against
it — there is no JS-observable error, and no argument to `loadExtension` or
`startWorkerForScope` changes the outcome.

nodes.title: Potential DLL Side-Loading Vulnerability in Electron 35 on Windows
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

35.0.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

win 11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Electron applications should not allow Windows system DLLs or optional DLLs to be loaded from the application installation directory unless explicitly intended. DLL loading should use secure Windows DLL loading mechanisms and trusted system locations to prevent DLL side-loading.

### Actual Behavior

The custom DLL is executed during application startup, resulting in arbitrary code execution (for example, Calculator launching from the DLL payload).

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

**Summary:**
- We observed behavior that may indicate a DLL side-loading vulnerability in Electron 30 on Windows.

**Environment**
- Electron: 35.0.0
- Platform: Windows 11 (64-bit)
- Packaging: Electron Forge (MSI)

**Steps to Reproduce**
- Build and install an Electron application.
- Monitor the application startup using Process Monitor.
- Observe that Windows probes the application installation directory for optional system DLLs, including:
   - CRYPTSP.dll

nodes.title: OSR useSharedTexture: details.texture is always null on Linux with the NVIDIA proprietary driver
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Electron Version 43.2.0 ### What operating system(s) are you using? Ubuntu ### Operating System Version Ubuntu 22.04.5 and Ubuntu 24.04.4, X11 (kernel 6.8.0-136) ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? I don't know how to test ### Expected Behavior With `webPreferences.offscreen.useSharedTexture: true`, the `paint` event should provide `details.texture` as an `OffscreenSharedTexture`, with `textureInfo.handle.nativePixmap.planes[].fd` on Linux. ### Actual Behavior `details.texture` is always `null` on Linux with the NVIDIA proprietary driver. The `paint` event fires normally, but every frame silently falls back to the CPU bitmap path, so the GPU-accelerated capture mode is unusable. There is no error thrown and no warning — the only way to notice is checking `details.texture` yourself. The same code returns a shared texture on Windows and macOS. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/sdkv2/94dec53fa8397ef82cd2e218dfdf9a36 ### Additional Information Reproduced on **Electron 43.2.0 and 40.10.6**, on four separate machines (RTX 3060), across both Ubuntu versions, three NVIDIA driver versions (575.51.03, 575.57.08, 580.95.05), two libgbm versions (23.2.1 and 25.2.8), and three X server setups (Xvfb, hand-configured Xorg with `nvidia_drv.so`, and a full SDDM/KDE session). Result was identical in every combination. `--enable-features=Vulkan` is often suggested as the NVIDIA workaround. It did not produce a shared texture in any configuration I tried, and it additionally disabled WebGL2 entirely — for an app using OSR to capture WebGL content, that trade is not usable. Note for anyone else testing this: Xvfb provides no DRI3, so it can never work — but hardware GL still reports a real GPU renderer string under it, which makes it look like a working setup.
In-depth investigation

`details.texture` is explicitly `null` rather than `undefined` (verified by dumping the whole paint callback: `arg[0] = { texture: null, preventDefault: …, defaultPrevented: false }`), so `offscreen_use_shared_texture_` is being set correctly in C++ — viz simply never delivers a usable frame to `OnFrameCaptured`. With `--enable-logging=stderr --v=1`, ANGLE reports: ``` ERROR:ui/gl/egl_util.cc:92] EGL Driver message (Error) : Internal Vulkan error (-8): A requested feature is not supported, in third_party/angle/src/libANGLE/renderer/vulkan/linux/DmaBufImageSiblingVkLinux.cpp, initImpl:616. ``` `-8` is `VK_ERROR_FEATURE_NOT_PRESENT`. (Line is `initImpl:616` on Electron 43.2.0 and `initImpl:614` on 40.10.6 — same function.) The likely cause is what the capture pool asks GBM for. `RenderableGpuMemoryBufferVideoFramePool` allocates with `requires_cpu_access = true` → `SCANOUT_CPU_READ_WRITE` → `GBM_BO_USE_LINEAR | GBM_BO_USE_SCANOUT | GBM_BO_USE_TEXTURING`, notably *without* `GBM_BO_USE_RENDERING` (`ui/gfx/linux/gbm_util.cc`). Chromium's own comment in `media/video/renderable_gpu_memory_buffer_video_frame_pool.cc` predicts this failure and names the vendor: > "On Linux, `GBM_BO_USE_LINEAR` (implied by `SCANOUT_CPU_READ_WRITE`) can prevent GPU rendering on some drivers, notably NVIDIA's GBM driver, because it disables `GBM_BO_USE_RENDERING`." So the buffer is allocated, but NVIDIA's Vulkan will not import a LINEAR/SCANOUT dma-buf as a renderable image sibling. Verified present on the failing hosts, so these are not the cause: - `nvidia-drm.modeset = Y`; `/dev/dri/card0` + `renderD128` present - X server exposes DRI2 + DRI3 - `nvidia-drm_gbm.so` GBM backend (`libnvidia-allocator`) - EGL: `EGL_EXT_image_dma_buf_import`, `EGL_EXT_image_dma_buf_import_modifiers`, `EGL_MESA_image_dma_buf_export` - Vulkan: `VK_EXT_image_drm_format_modifier` (rev 2), `VK_EXT_external_memory_dma_buf`, `VK_EXT_queue_family_foreign`, `VK_KHR_external_memory_fd` - `app.getGPUFeatureStatus()` at paint time: `gpu_compositing=enabled vulkan=enabled_on webgl=enabled opengl=enabled_on rasterization=enabled_force` Ruled out: - All four `sharedTexturePixelFormat` values (`argb`, `nv12`, `rgba`, `bgra`) — identical result. - `--enable-native-gpu-memory-buffers` — no effect; it gates the client-side mmap path (`ui/gfx/linux/client_native_pixmap_dmabuf.cc`), while the viz capture pool uses `always_create_native_gmb_handle=true` and never consults it. - `--use-angle=gl` vs `--use-angle=vulkan` — no effect (both report the same ANGLE/Vulkan renderer on these hosts). - Initially-hidden window — `paintWhenInitiallyHidden: true` is set and `paint` does fire. The Linux `NativePixmapHandle` branch in `shell/browser/osr/osr_video_consumer.cc` looks correct, so this does not appear to be missing Electron code — the mismatch is upstream, between what the capture pool requests and what NVIDIA's GBM/Vulkan will import. Filing here because this is where it surfaces and because `docs/api/structures/shared-texture-handle.md` lists `nativePixmap` as Linux-supported without noting it does not work on the NVIDIA proprietary driver. Possibly related: #49247.

nodes.title: [Bug]: macOS 26.4 (Tahoe): browser process never exits after quit if a BrowserWindow was ever created — infinite usleep poll loop after all teardown completes
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the Contributing Guidelines for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the Code of Conduct that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the issue tracker for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

43.2.0 (also reproduced on 42.8.0, 43.1.0, and 44.0.0-alpha.8 — see below)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.4.1 (Tahoe)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

None on macOS 26.4.1 — every version tested (42.8.0, 43.1.0, 43.2.0, 44.0.0-alpha.8) hangs 5/5. The same versions exit cleanly on earlier macOS, so the regression is OS-version-gated, not Electron-version-gated.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Unknown — not systematically tested. The stall is in Electron Framework code (unsymbolicated Chromium teardown frames), so Chrome may carry a different shutdown path or a fix.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/bofeizhu/f91f42f580632ecff84b393ef939e66a (both mains, the EXIT/HANG runner, and the full `sample` output of a hanging 44.0.0-alpha.8 process)

### Expected Behavior

After `app.quit()` completes, the process exits.

### Actual Behavior

If the app **ever created a BrowserWindow** (even a single hidden one that only loaded `about:blank`), the main process never exits after quitting. The window closes, the Dock entry disappears, every JS lifecycle stage completes normally in milliseconds — `before-quit`, window close, `will-quit`, `quit`, and even Node's `process.on('exit')` — and the process then idles forever holding 100–150 MB RSS, spinning in a native usleep poll loop, at ~0% CPU.

With **no window at all**, the identical quit path exits cleanly with code 0 in ~1 s, 5/5.

Key observations:

- **Unbounded**: the process is still alive after 6.5 minutes; there is no timeout guard. Only SIGKILL ends it.
- **It is not waiting on children**: during the hang, the renderer helper exits first, then the GPU process and NetworkService utility helpers exit on their own within the first minute. After that the browser process is completely alone — no children, no windows — and still never exits.
- **Emergency exits hang identically**: calling `process.exit(0)` or `app.exit(0)` from the `quit` event produces the same stall, so the loop runs during native `exit()`/atexit/static-destructor teardown, past the last point where JS can run.
- **Stack signature**: `sample <pid>` during the hang shows 100% of samples (2612/2612 over 3 s) on the main thread in the identical stack — a chain of unsymbolicated Electron Framework frames with the leaf in `usleep` (libsystem_c). No modal/NSAlert, no dispatch-queue wait. Sample file attached.
- Reproduced 5/5 on each of Electron 42.8.0, 43.1.0, 43.2.0, and 44.0.0-alpha.8, in two independent investigation sessions on separate days.

Because the trigger is "a scene-backed NSWindow existed at some point," this looks like the macOS 26 scene-window teardown family (cf. #52437, which is a *different* signature: a runtime `performAsyncAndWait` dispatch deadlock while the app is unresponsive — here the app is responsive to the end, all teardown succeeds, and only the final process exit stalls). Also distinct from #49261 (macOS force-SIGKILLing running Electron apps). Presumably some teardown routine polls for a scene/WindowServer acknowledgment that macOS 26.4 no longer delivers.

### Steps to Reproduce

`main-hidden.js` — hangs 5/5:

```js
const { app, BrowserWindow } = require('electron');

app.whenReady().then(async () => {
  const win = new BrowserWindow({ show: false });
  await win.loadURL('about:blank');
  setTimeout(() => app.quit(), 500);
});

app.on('window-all-closed', () => app.quit());
app.on('quit', () => console.log('QUIT_EVENT_FIRED'));
```

`main-nowindow.js` — control, exits cleanly 5/5:

```js
const { app } = require('electron');

app.whenReady().then(() => {
  setTimeout(() => app.quit(), 500);
});

app.on('quit', () => console.log('QUIT_EVENT_FIRED'));
```

1. On macOS 26.4.x (arm64), `npm i electron@43.2.0` (or any version listed above).
2. `./node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron main-hidden.js`
3. Observe `QUIT_EVENT_FIRED` printed at ~900 ms; the command never returns. `ps` shows the process alive at ~0% CPU indefinitely; `sample` shows the usleep poll loop.
4. Run `main-nowindow.js` the same way: exits with code 0 in ~1 s.

A small runner that spawns Electron N times and reports EXIT/HANG with timings is included in the gist (`run.js`).

### Additional Information

- Real-world impact: any Electron app on macOS 26.4 leaves a zombie main process holding hundreds of MB every time the user quits. We currently work around it by SIGKILLing our own process from the `quit` event.
- Happy to re-run the harness against any branch/build that might help bisect.
